title: Finite scalar presentation under internal-module transport
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], $R=\Lambda(*)$ its reconstructed ordinary scalar ring [def-zl-t-admissible-coefficient-models], and $X$ any scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Let $F_X$ be the ordinary realization defined in [lem-zl-flat-condensed-scalar-realization] (the construction, without its flatness assumption). Let $R_{\mathrm{int}}$ be the internal scalar ring object of abelian groups and $E_X$ the finite-constant scalar-extension functor of [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]. For any internal $\Lambda_X$-module sheaf $M$, the following are equivalent: (i) there is a finitely presented ordinary $R$-module $N$ and an isomorphism $M\cong F_X(N)$; (ii) there is an internal $R_{\mathrm{int}}$-module $P$ which is a cokernel of a map between finite direct sums of the regular module, and an isomorphism $M\cong E_X(P)$. No flatness, coherence, regularity or geometric component hypothesis is assumed.

source.place: Section 3, formula (3.1), Remark 3.2, proof of Theorem 6.2(2), and equation (6.2)

proof.text: The unique isomorphism from the explicitly chosen one-point profinite set to the chosen terminal object identifies its Lambda section ring with R, including multiplication and the unit. The internal-module/ordinary-module equivalence converts an action gamma to r*x=gamma(r tensor x). It sends the regular module to R and finite direct sums to finite free modules. Both directions preserve cokernels. A presentation R^m -> R^n -> N -> 0 therefore gives an internal finite presentation, and every internal finite presentation becomes such an ordinary presentation. This includes m=0, n=0 and the zero ring.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 6.2(2), using (3.1), Remark 3.2, (6.2), and Proposition 6.6

proof.text: Compare constant modules before and after section reconstruction: both are sheafifications of the constant module presheaf with the original scalar action. Their sheafification units identify them uniquely. The two coefficient maps are the constant-section adjunction counit, so they agree under the terminal-object identification of Step 1. The normalized internal/sectionwise scalar-adjunction comparison sends s tensor n to s tensor n; its inverse is the same generator formula in the opposite convention. Thus ordinary scalar extensions agree naturally. Apply the sectionwise/internal inverse equivalence and inverse image to X.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 6.2(2), using (3.1), Remark 3.2, (6.2), and Proposition 6.6

proof.text: For (i), apply the inverse scalar-module equivalence to N, use Step 1 for finite presentation, and compose the isomorphism of Step 2 with M isomorphic to F_X(N). For (ii), apply the forward equivalence to P, use Step 1, and use the inverse comparison of Step 2. Neither direction requires a uniform choice across different covering members.

lean.statement:
theorem ordinaryScalarRealization_finitePresentation
    (Λ : Profinite.CondensedRing.{u}) [IsCommMonObj Λ.X] (X : Scheme.{u})
    (M : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj Λ.X X)) :
    (∃ N : ModuleCat.{u + 1} (scalarRing Λ), Module.FinitePresentation (scalarRing Λ) N ∧
      Nonempty (M ≅ (ordinaryScalarRealization Λ X).obj N)) ↔
    (∃ P : Mod Ab.{u + 1} (scalarRingObj Λ.X),
      Mod.IsFinitelyPresented (scalarRingObj Λ.X) P ∧
      Nonempty (M ≅ (finiteConstantScalarExtension Λ.X X).obj P))
